chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about the sacrifice (al-adha): Is it obligatory upon the one who finds the means for himself and his dependents? So he said: As for himself, he should not leave it; and as for his dependents, if he wishes, he can leave it.

key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: The ritual animal sacrifice, typically performed during Eid al-Adha
key_terms.عِيَالِهِ: His dependents (family members supported by him)

ai.seo_question: Is the ritual sacrifice obligatory for one's dependents?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the personal obligation of the sacrifice for the head of the household and the discretionary nature for his dependents, reflecting the Shia juristic view that while it is highly emphasized for the owner, it is not strictly mandatory for others in the family unit. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Islamic worship, allowing the provider to prioritize financial resources based on household needs while maintaining the spiritual practice. The distinction underscores the principle that religious duties scale with individual capacity and role within the family structure.
